title: Physical path components in the daemon namespace
scope: Absolute namespace lookup and mutation paths traverse dot and dot-dot components in physical order; dot-dot clamps at the selected World root
Repeated interior slashes are accepted, while a trailing slash remains unsupported
Terminal dot and dot-dot components may be looked up but are rejected for mutation so reserved names cannot become directory entries
Missing prefixes and dot-dot traversal through a regular file fail; path and component byte limits remain 4096 and 255 bytes
Directory inode path hints discard noncanonical physical aliases before RPC child paths are constructed
Namespace verification and revision diff reject corrupt stored entry names including dot, dot-dot, slash-containing, and repeated-slash names
explicit_exclusions: This is daemon C++ Namespace and raw-RPC behavior only; it does not claim native filesystem path semantics or a new mount capability
No lexical normalization across symlinks is claimed; traversal follows the symlink before processing later dot-dot components
